title: Investigate and mitigate cross-namespace slab-tearing leading to sustained KV cache memory growth
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a capacity event on 2026-03-09 we observed persistent growth of memory allocated to the KV prefix cache for multiple tenants. The cache did not return to baseline after load normalized and required rolling restarts to reclaim memory. This ticket captures investigation notes, interim mitigations, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: High: Several production routes experienced degraded latency and increased OOM risk. Two customers on Dedicated capacity reported SLA alerts. Total affected hosts: 18, across 3 regions. No customer data exposure identified.
reproduction_steps: Load test with sustained high-variance prefix churn (mix of small and large keys, TTLs 30s-24h) against a cluster configured with 8GB cache per shard.
Simulate concurrent eviction and insert workload with artificially constrained eviction iteration budget (set EVICITON_MAX_ITER low) to increase eviction pressure.
Run the internal slab-reuse debug build that enables allocation stack traces and run until memory growth observed (~12-24 hours in test harness).
observed_behavior: Memory usage of the cache grows monotonically despite eviction callbacks indicating entries were removed. Heap allocations attributed to 'prefix slab allocator' increase; slab free lists show non-zero free_count but free bytes are not reclaimed. Reference-count metrics reported occasional negative transient values during heavy churn, suggesting a race where refcount is decremented twice.
hypothesis_root_cause: A race between prefix insertion and concurrent eviction/compaction path leaves 'ghost' slab segments referenced by hash table entries. The ghost entries fail fast-path removal due to a missed tombstone write in the prefix index after rehashing during background compaction. The allocator's slab reuse path can mark freed memory as free_count>0 while the hash bucket still holds a stale pointer; later re-insertions allocate new chunks instead of reusing, causing fragmentation and apparent leak. Contributing factors: (1) compaction/rehash code assumes single-writer to a bucket, (2) eviction concurrency budget was lowered in a prior perf change (ENG-70213) leading to incomplete eviction sweeps under high churn, (3) missing guard in reference-counting updates allowing double-decrement on a rare path.
root_cause_summary: Concurrency regression in the prefix cache compaction/eviction codepath that allowed stale pointers into slab memory to persist while the allocator also returned those slabs to free lists, producing fragmentation and sustained memory growth. A previous optimization that reduced eviction sweep aggressiveness amplified the window for this race.
action_items: Immediate patch: Add a global per-bucket compaction lock (lightweight spin) to guarantee single writer during rehash/evict. Owner: Marco Ruiz. ETA: 2026-03-17.
Telemetry: Emit 'bucket_mutation_seq' monotonic counter and 'tombstone_write_success' boolean for each rehash/evict operation. Owner: Priya Shah. ETA: 2026-03-20.
Reference-count hardening: Fail-fast assert in debug builds when refcount would go negative; add atomic RCU-style increments on insert path. Owner: Wei Zhang. ETA: 2026-03-24.
Eviction policy revert: Temporarily restore previous eviction sweep budget for all clusters while we validate fixes (rollback ENG-70213 change). Owner: SRE runbook owners. ETA: 2026-03-15.
End-to-end fuzzing: Add targeted concurrency fuzz tests to our CI that simulate inserts+evicts+compaction at varying delays. Owner: QA infra (Lena Ortiz). ETA: 2026-03-31.
Backfill unit tests: Add unit tests that assert no stale pointers after forced rehashes and that free lists are empty after full eviction pass. Owner: Marco Ruiz. ETA: 2026-03-22.

Runbook update: Document detection query and mitigation steps (soft restart the cache service shard, increase eviction budget, enable debug trace) and attach to postmortem. Owner: On-call SRE. ETA: 2026-03-18.

Customer communication: Notify affected Dedicated customers of fixes and provide recommended mitigations for self-hosted deployments (rolling restart). Owner: Customer Ops (Riley Kim). ETA: 2026-03-19.

Post-deploy validation: 72-hour canary with memory/eviction telemetry thresholds and automatic rollback if growth > 8% sustained. Owner: Release Engineer (Diego Alvarez). ETA: included in release plan runtime-1.20.
Long-term: Explore slab allocator redesign to include quarantine epoch before reuse to avoid reuse-of-freed-memory races. Owner: Research/Applied ML infra (Dr. Elena Novak). ETA: Q3 2026.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Triage call with SRE, Runtime, and QA. Captured initial heap profile and enabled extended debug traces in canary cluster.
2026-03-11: Confirmed reproduction in local fuzz harness. Observed negative refcount assertion in debug build on 2/1000 runs.
2026-03-12: Rolled temporary eviction budget rollback to all production clusters (reverted prior perf tweak); saw memory growth plateau on 6/8 affected hosts within 3 hours.
2026-03-13: Implemented and smoke-tested per-bucket compaction lock in staging; no measurable latency regression on synthetic QPS-1000 test.
2026-03-14: Patch submitted: PR #12487. Running extended integration test with concurrency fuzzing job (48h run).
review_feedback: PM (Samir Gupta): Ensure customer-facing remediation notes include explicit rollback guidance and expected RTO for rolling restarts.
Security (Jordan Lee): Confirm that debug traces do not leak key material; scrubbed traces validated by Security team.
Design (Maya Chen): Add dashboard widget and alert for 'bucket_mutation_seq' divergence to Console release plan.
SRE (Kim Nguyen): Request post-deploy runbook test during canary window to validate automated rollback triggers.
blockers: Need sign-off from SRE to apply global eviction budget rollback cluster-wide (open change window).
Extended fuzzing run must complete without flake to accept concurrency lock approach (48h canary).
resolution_notes: Pending: temporary rollback to previous eviction budget stabilized memory while we validated compaction-lock patch. If canary passes, we will ship the compaction-lock + reference-count hardening in runtime-1.20. Rolling restarts were performed for two affected Dedicated customers to immediately reclaim memory. Full remediation requires the unit tests and fuzzing coverage merged to prevent regression.
notes_for_followup: Verify that the semaphore-based bucket lock scales on 256-concurrency workloads — if not, replace with per-bucket RW lock and optimize hot-bucket fast-path.
Schedule a follow-up audit of allocator changes in Q2 to measure fragmentation characteristics across real customer workloads.
Add postmortem card to retro: what changes allowed reduced eviction sweep aggressiveness without additional safety checks?
